# Tutorial: create a web app for this project and put it on the tailnet

You are a Claude session working inside this project folder. Follow this
tutorial when the user asks you to "create a web (by the tutorial)". The goal:
a web app for this project, reachable from the user's phone/laptop at

```
https://desktop-6564cab.tailddc22a.ts.net/app/<name>
```

That URL is served by Tailscale (TLS included) and is reachable **only from
devices inside the user's tailnet VPN** - nothing becomes public.

## Step 1 - pick a name and a port

- **Name:** use `move-it` for this project. The console matches a published
  mount back to this project by that exact name (lowercase folder name), so a
  different name means the project's **Web** button will not find the app.
- **Port:** pick one in **8100-8699** and confirm it is free:

```powershell
Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
# no output = free
```

Never use **8787** - that is the RADC console itself. Do not touch its process,
its scheduled tasks, or the root `/` mount in Tailscale Serve.

## Step 2 - build the web app

Build whatever the user asked for inside this project folder (static site,
Vite/React app, small API - user's choice wins over any default here).

**Critical constraint - the URL prefix is stripped.** A request to
`/app/move-it/sub/page` reaches your server as `/sub/page`. Therefore:

- Use **relative** URLs (`./style.css`, not `/style.css`) in static HTML, or
- set the base path in your bundler (Vite: `base: '/app/move-it/'` in
  `vite.config.ts`; Next.js: `basePath: '/app/move-it'` in `next.config.js`)
  so built asset links and redirects resolve under the mount.

An absolute redirect or link that ignores the prefix (e.g. `/login`) escapes
the mount and lands on the console instead of your app. Plain JSON APIs need
nothing special.

## Step 3 - serve it on 127.0.0.1:<port>

Bind to **127.0.0.1** (not 0.0.0.0). Examples:

```powershell
$env:Path = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\nodejs;$env:Path"
# Vite dev:            npm run dev -- --port <port>
# Vite build + static: npx vite preview --port <port>
# Plain node server:   node server.js   (listen on 127.0.0.1:<port>)
```

Note: a server started inside this terminal session dies when the session
closes. For a quick demo that is fine. If the user wants it to stay up, start
it as a detached process (e.g. `Start-Process -WindowStyle Hidden node server.js`)
and tell the user it will not survive a reboot unless a scheduled task is added.
The console shows the **Web** button as unavailable whenever the port stops
answering, so a stopped app is visible rather than a broken link.

## Step 4 - expose it

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File D:\remote-ai-dev-console\scripts\expose-web.ps1 -Name move-it -Port <port>
```

The script mounts `/app/move-it` in Tailscale Serve and probes the URL. No RADC
restart is involved and none is allowed.

## Step 5 - verify and hand over

```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest https://desktop-6564cab.tailddc22a.ts.net/app/move-it -UseBasicParsing | Select-Object -ExpandProperty StatusCode   # expect 200
```

Then give the user the full URL. Remind them it only works on devices logged
into their Tailscale VPN. The project's **Web** button in the console appears
as soon as the mount exists and the port answers.

## Managing mounts

```powershell
# list everything currently published
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File D:\remote-ai-dev-console\scripts\list-web.ps1

# remove this app's mount (never touches the RADC root)
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File D:\remote-ai-dev-console\scripts\unexpose-web.ps1 -Name move-it
```

After removal the URL no longer serves anything: the console answers it with a
"no web app published here" page instead of its own UI, so a dead mount can
never be mistaken for the app. Use `list-web.ps1` as the source of truth.
